KEY MESSAGE 1...As of 2:10 PM EDT...Current radar imagery shows
some isolated to scattered showers that have developed over the
last hour or so across the upper Hudson Valley. These showers 
are associated with an area of locally enhanced low-level 
convergence and relatively higher dew points per latest NYS 
mesonet obs. A weak upper shortwave tracking to the north is 
also adding some enhanced lift. Current SPC mesoanalysis shows a
tongue of 500-1000 J/KG of MLCAPE extending down the 
Champlain/upper Hudson Valley area, so would not be surprised to
see some thunder as well across northern areas through the next
few hours. Low-level shear is unimpressive although deep-layer 
shear is more favorable for the upper Hudson Valley into 
southern VT. SPC has kept our area in just a general thunder 
risk this afternoon, but we can't totally rule out a few 
instances of gusty winds or even some hail for northern areas 
through the next few hours. That said, threat is isolated at 
best with lack of large-scale forcing and very low DCAPE values.


Better forcing arrives this evening into early tonight as another 
upper shortwave approaches from the west along with some 
increasing low-level theta e advection. Main focus will be for 
areas south of I- 90, for the southeastern Catskills and Mid 
Hudson Valley where an area/cluster of showers and storms is 
expected to track late this evening into tonight, departing into
New England by late tonight. 12z HREF suggests SBCAPE values 
increasing to 500-1000 J/KG this evening for this area, while 
strengthening NW flow aloft will lead to increasing deep-layer 
shear up to 40-45 kt. Instability should start to wane after 
sunset as convection approaches from the west, which should 
prevent a widespread severe threat. SPC has a marginal risk for 
severe storms just to our west where the timing looks more 
favorable for severe weather. However, a few stronger storms 
can't be ruled out across the southeastern Catskills into the 
southern Mid Hudson Valley given the modest instability and 
increasing shear. Main hazard would be gusty winds, but with WBZ
heights near or just below 10 kft and long straight hodographs,
some marginally severe hail is also on the table this evening 
for these areas. 

Will also mention increasing signal for some heavy downpours with 
this area of thunderstorms this evening into tonight. Storm 
motions should be fast with strengthening flow aloft, but some 
training appears possible with unidirectional flow parallel to 
a weak frontal boundary. CAMs have started to come around to 
this idea, with the 12z HREF suggesting a 50% chance for >1" of
rain in 3 hrs for the Mid Hudson Valley tonight with some 
1-1.5" rainfall totals showing up in the PM. Fortunately, this 
looks more like a nuisance ponding of water type situation vs a 
flash flood threat with FFG values >1.75" in 1 hr for our 
southern counties.

While main batch of showers will track off to the east prior to 
sunrise tomorrow morning, some redevelopment of showers and storms 
is possible tomorrow afternoon with another upper shortwave and cold 
pool aloft tracking just north of the International Border. 12z HREF 
is suggesting up to 750-1000 J/KG of SBCAPE again for northern 
areas tomorrow overlapping with very strong deep-layer shear. 
However, questions remain about strength of the forcing and 
abundant mid-level dry air that may stifle convection. So, 
while threat is very conditional upon updrafts being able to get
going tomorrow, a few stronger storms with gusty winds and/or 
marginally severe hail again are possible for the southeastern 
ADKs, upper Hudson Valley, and/or southern VT. SPC has kept us 
in a general thunder risk for now given the lackluster forcing 
and mid-level drying/subsidence. Will continue to evaluate 
guidance over the next 12-24 hrs and collaborate with SPC if an 
upgrade to a marginal risk may be warranted.


KEY MESSAGE 2...On Friday, a strong cold front will track across 
our region as a fairly strong upper shortwave dives southeastwards 
across NY. Despite the fairly strong forcing, capping aloft and
lack of moisture should result in, at most, just a few isolated
showers with the frontal passage. High pressure then builds 
into the region behind the front Friday night, remaining 
overhead into Sunday morning. Accordingly, have lowered temps 
from the NBM for western areas Friday night with favorable 
radiational cooling conditions expected. Low generally will be 
in the 50s for valley areas and low to mid 40s for the high 
terrain. Saturday looks like a gorgeous late-summer day with 
low humidity, mainly clear skies, and highs in the 70s. Latest 
guidance has trended slightly slower with the departure of the 
sfc high, so Saturday night will also likely feature lows in the
40s to 50s.
